_comment: How the Django suite is split across CI jobs. One source of truth, read
twice: .github/workflows/ci.yml turns a shard index into test labels with
jq, and core/tests/test_shard_partition.py proves the split still covers
every test. JSON rather than a Python module because georiva/__init__.py
imports celery, and the CI runner resolving these labels has no celery.
Balanced by measured time, not by test count — the two disagree sharply,
and a change to what a test costs moves them: the switch to a fast test
password hasher cut organisations from 170s to 24s but ingestion only
from 89s to 37s, which left the old split at 40s, 25s and 84s.
Per-app test seconds when this was last measured, from CI's own per-test
timestamps (run 40853392114). Re-measure before trusting them; the useful
part is the ratios:
ingestion 37 | sources 36 | organisations 24 | core 17 | wmts 10
processing 9 | events   7 | virtual_zarr   6 | everything else ~4
That puts the shards at about 40s, 61s and 47s. ingestion and sources
are the two big blocks and belong on different shards; the slowest shard
cannot drop below about 60s without splitting an app.
Shard 0 is deliberately the lightest. It carries the work no other shard
repeats — the prod image build, the missing-migration check, and the only
write of the build cache — so its tests have to fit in the slack, or those
extras land on the critical path.
Apps may be left out only if they hold no tests. Nothing enforces the
balance, but the guard test enforces the coverage: add a test to an app
named in no shard and it fails.
